records.summary: The managed third-party drift alert remained open after the pinned dependency matched upstream and required manual reconciliation.

records.title: Reconcile resolved managed drift alerts
records.problem: The accepted drift workflow can open or refresh an alert but does not close a managed alert when exact drift disappears.
records.owner_outcome: Keep the issue ledger current without closing manual issues or changing updater policy.

records.claim: The versioned synthetic suite retains the current open-or-refresh behavior and the missing managed no-drift close case.
records.limitations: The suite is a public control model and does not execute GitHub writes or prove live issue permissions.

records.claim: The synthetic candidate satisfies all three lifecycle cases while the current baseline leaves the resolved managed alert open.
records.limitations: The evaluation-only run establishes contract behavior only; it is not implementation, owner-live value, or permission evidence.

records.title: Managed third-party drift alert reconciliation
records.problem: Resolved auto-managed drift alerts can remain stale after the manifest again matches upstream.
records.owner_outcome: Remove stale managed alerts without hiding real drift or touching manual issues.
records.hypothesis: A marker-bound, exact-no-drift reconciliation step can close only resolved managed alerts while preserving all manual and active alerts.
alternatives: Keep manual closure as the accepted baseline
Add marker-bound reconciliation in a separately reviewed epic
Close every matching-title issue without provenance checks

reuse_build_reject.reuse: Reuse the accepted third-party manifest and drift result as the only state input.
reuse_build_reject.build: Build only the separately scoped issue #836 after its own review and tests.
reuse_build_reject.reject: Reject title-only closure, direct implementation from this RFC, and any updater-policy change.

authority.details: The RFC may open a separate epic but cannot close issues, merge, deploy, or authorize implementation.

security.details: Any later implementation must require exact automation provenance and a current no-drift result.

privacy.details: Only synthetic-public state cases and public repository metadata are retained.

data_retention.details: Evidence remains in repository history; no owner or provider data is collected.

license.details: No external code or dependency is copied.

supply_chain.details: The evidence package adds no executable dependency or update path.

compatibility.details: The proposal preserves the accepted manifest and updater policy and is separately reversible.

benchmark.falsification_plan: Reject the proposal if it closes an unmarked issue, closes while drift remains, or cannot improve the retained managed no-drift case.

prototype_disposition.reason: A synthetic decision-table comparison is sufficient to scope an epic; live GitHub writes are deliberately excluded.

outcome_history.reason: The separately scoped epic remains unscheduled and has produced no implementation outcome.

migration.plan: This RFC changes no workflow or issue state; any later epic must define its own migration boundary.

rollback.plan: Preserve this accepted record; if later evidence falsifies it, close issue #836 and append an evidence-bound negative outcome rather than rewriting history.

records.rationale: Public repository evidence and the synthetic E9 comparison justify only a separately reviewed, unscheduled epic.
records.reconsideration_trigger: New evidence that provenance cannot safely distinguish managed alerts, or that no-drift closure hides an active failure.

acceptance_criteria: Close only an exact auto-managed alert after an exact current no-drift result.
Never close a manual, unmarked, ambiguous, or actively drifting issue.

records.summary: The accepted precursor catalogue retained replacing Nerva's brain with an external agent framework as a radical rejected hypothesis.

records.title: Replace the Nerva control plane with an external framework
records.problem: A clean-sheet external framework could appear simpler than preserving Nerva's existing local-first control contracts.
records.owner_outcome: Test the radical alternative without weakening authority, privacy, migration, or rollback evidence.

records.claim: The synthetic suite pins the accepted control-plane invariants that a radical replacement would have to preserve.
records.limitations: The suite represents repository contracts; it does not evaluate every external framework or future version.

records.claim: The radical replacement model violates all four retained authority, locality, delivery, and rollback cases while the simple baseline preserves them.
records.limitations: The result rejects this broad control-plane replacement hypothesis, not every bounded adapter or reuse proposal.

records.title: External framework as Nerva control-plane replacement
records.problem: Replacing the established control plane could erase local-only routing, action authority, delivery separation, and reversible migration contracts.
records.owner_outcome: Reject broad replacement unless new evidence proves all accepted controls and a measurable benefit.
records.hypothesis: A generic external agent framework can replace the Nerva control plane while preserving every accepted invariant and outperforming the simple baseline.
alternatives: Retain the current Nerva control boundary
Reuse bounded external components behind existing adapters
Replace the full control plane with an external framework

reuse_build_reject.reuse: Permit future bounded adapters only through their own E8 and architecture reviews.
reuse_build_reject.build: Build no replacement or prototype from this rejected RFC.
reuse_build_reject.reject: Reject the broad control-plane replacement because it fails the retained invariant baseline.

authority.details: The broad replacement does not preserve the sole privileged-action and no-direct-delivery boundaries.

security.details: Replacing the control plane creates an unjustified expansion of trusted execution and policy surface.

privacy.details: The evidence is synthetic-public; no owner data or external framework input is used.

data_retention.details: Only immutable repository evidence is retained.

license.details: No specific external package is admitted; any future bounded candidate requires its own exact license review.

supply_chain.details: No external code is fetched or executed; future reuse requires exact provenance and dependency review.

compatibility.details: The radical replacement fails compatibility with the retained authority and routing contracts.

benchmark.falsification_plan: Reject unless a new candidate preserves every authority, locality, delivery, and rollback invariant and then beats the retained baseline.

prototype_disposition.reason: The contract-level negative result falsifies the broad hypothesis before external code ingestion or execution is justified.

outcome_history.reason: A rejected RFC creates no epic, implementation, or outcome claim.

migration.plan: No replacement is implemented and no runtime or stored state changes.

rollback.plan: Preserve the rejection; reconsider only through a new revision with genuinely new post-decision evidence.

records.rationale: The radical replacement fails every retained control invariant in the synthetic benchmark and provides no evidence for weakening the simple baseline.
records.reconsideration_trigger: A new exact candidate and independent evidence that preserve all four control invariants and demonstrate measurable benefit over the retained baseline.
